ranking.note: Raised from P2: trimmed package txs entering peer reject filters censors legitimate CPFP fee-bumps until the next block, which is the pinning/package-relay resistance the category ranks first and that L2 depends on.
Kept P3 but placed last in band: author states it is a draft accompanying unaccepted BIP proposals and vendors unmerged libsecp changes, so the mempool-policy value is speculative.

inconsistencies: #36182 and #36317 both change the mempool fee estimator's view of what counts as mined/usable data and will likely touch the same accounting code; review #36182 first (it fixes the user-visible underestimation path), then #36317 on top.

#36367 (cluster FeeFrac overflow via prioritisetransaction) and #36214 (cluster trimming during reorgs) both exercise cluster mempool invariants; #36367 fixes an actual overflow and should be reviewed before the test-only #36214, whose coverage may need updating afterwards.

#35286 (testsubmitpackage dry-run) and #36328 (package trimming result codes) both concern package acceptance result semantics; #36328's change to TX_RECONSIDERABLE affects what the new RPC would report, so it should land or be decided first.
#35581 is driven by mining's waitNext rather than mempool policy itself; its mempool-side value is the MempoolUpdated/fee-diagram signal, so its priority here rests only on that plumbing.
result.notes: No P1 cluster of bugs here apart from #36328; the rest of the bug fixes are genuine but bounded (fee-estimator accounting, reorg eviction, operator-triggered overflow), so they sit together in P2. The two test-coverage PRs differ: #36214 covers the cluster mempool project the category calls out, so it stays P3, while #35882 only tightens reject-string assertions on already-covered rules and stays P4.
